en: Catalogue of the Scriptures, Volume One:
Single Texts. Originally there was one version, with no other translations;
totaling three hundred and seventy works in one thousand seven hundred and eighty-six fascicles.
Mahāyāna Sūtras as Single Texts: One Hundred and Fifty-nine Works in Five Hundred and Fifty-eight Fascicles.
*The Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra*, sixty fascicles (or fifty fascicles), translated at Yangzhou by Buddhabhadra together with Faye and others during the Yixi era of the Jin dynasty.

*The Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*, forty fascicles, translated at Guzang by Dharmakṣema together with Huisong and others during the Juqu reign of the Northern Liang dynasty. *The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, forty fascicles (or thirty fascicles).

During the Later Qin dynasty, Kumārajīva, together with Sengrui and others, translated the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* (also known as the *Mahāvaipulya-mahāsannipāta-sūtra*) in thirty fascicles at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an.
During the Northern Liang dynasty, Dharmakṣema translated the *Mahāvaipulya-sūryagarbha-sūtra* in fifteen fascicles at Guzang.
During the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui dynasty, Jñānayaśas translated the *Mahāvaipulya-candragarbha-sūtra* in ten fascicles at Daxingshan Temple.
The *Bodhisattva-alaṃkāra-sūtra* in thirteen (or fourteen) fascicles was translated during the Qi dynasty by Dharmayaśas;
the *Bodhisattva-darśana-tattva-samādhi-sūtra* in fourteen fascicles was translated at Chang’an by Zhu Fonian in the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin;
and the *Buddhanāma-sūtra* in twelve fascicles was translated during the Qi dynasty by Dharmayaśas.
During the Northern Wei dynasty, Bodhiruci translated the *Candrapradīpa-samādhi-sūtra* in ten fascicles at Xiangzhou.
During the Tiāntǒng era of the Qi dynasty, Dharmayaśas, together with Fazhi, translated the *Bhadrakalpika-sūtra* in thirteen fascicles.
During the Yuánkāng era of the Jin dynasty, Dharmarakṣa translated the *Puṣpavyūha-sūtra* in ten, twelve, or eleven fascicles.
During the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty, Kumārajīva translated the *Mahāvaipulya-candragarbha-sūtra* in ten fascicles at the Great Monastery in Chang’an.
During the Qi dynasty, Narendrayaśas and others retranslated the *Daśabhūmi-vibhāṣā-śāstra* (or *Daśabhūmi-karmasaṃgraha-sūtra*) in ten fascicles.
During the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin dynasty, Zhu Fonian, together with Dao’an, translated the *Mahābhiṣeka-sūtra* in nine or twelve fascicles.
The *Buddhanusmṛti-samādhi Sūtra* in eight fascicles was translated during the Jin dynasty by Śrīmitra.
The *Suvikrāntavikrami-paripṛcchā-prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* in seven fascicles was translated at Yangzhou during the Yongchu era of the Song dynasty by Buddhabhadra.
The *Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra* in six or seven fascicles was translated at Yangzhou during the Chen dynasty by the prince of the Yuezhi kingdom, Vasurendra.
The latter three fascicles were translated by Dharmakṣema during the Northern Liang period; the *Ratnamegha-sūtra* in seven fascicles was translated by Paramārtha during the Chen period;
the *Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra* in six or seven fascicles was translated by Mandaraka in Yangzhou during the Liang period;
and the *Bodhisattvagarbha-sūtra* in five fascicles was translated by Bodhiruci in Luoyang during the Later Wei period.
During the Former Qin dynasty, Zhu Fonian translated the *Śraddhābalādhānāvatāramukha-dharmaparyāya-sūtra* in five fascicles at Chang’an.
During the Later Wei dynasty, Bodhiruci translated the *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra* in five fascicles.
In the Tiāntǒng era of the Qi dynasty, Dharmayaśas, together with Fazhi, translated the *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra* in five fascicles at Xiangzhou.
During the Northern Wei dynasty, Bodhiruci translated the *Nianfo Sanmei Jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Buddha-Recollection) in five or six fascicles at Luoyang.

During the Daming era of the Song dynasty, Gongde Zhi translated the *Dafangdeng Wuxiang Jing* (Mahāvaipulya Sūtra on the Signless), in six fascicles—also known as the *Dayun Jing* (Great Cloud Sūtra)—at Yangzhou.
During the Former Qin dynasty, Zhu Fonian translated the *Miji Jingang Lishi Jing* (Sūtra of the Vajrapāṇi Guhyapada) in four fascicles at Chang’an.
The *Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra* in four fascicles, translated by Zhu Fahu during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty;
the *Sāgaranāgarāja Sūtra* in four fascicles, translated by Faqun at Gaochang Commandery during the Northern Liang dynasty;
and the *Aṅgulimālīya Sūtra* in four fascicles, translated by Dharmakṣema during the Northern Liang dynasty.
In the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty, Guṇabhadra translated the *Saṃghāṭa-sūtra* in four fascicles at Yangzhou.
During the Northern Wei period, Upaśūna translated the *Sarvabuddhaguṇavyūha-sūtra* in three fascicles.
In the Hongshi era of the Later Qin, Kumārajīva translated the *Samādhirāja-sūtra* (also known as the *Bodhisattvapṛcchā-samādhi-sūtra*) in either three or two fascicles.
The *Bodhisattvapitaka-sūtra* in three fascicles, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty;
the *Balādhāna-samādhi-sūtra* in three fascicles, translated by Kumārajīva in the Hongshi era of the Later Qin;
and the *Pañcāśatsāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-parīkṣā-sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by Jñānayaśas during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui.
The *Sūtra of the Devaputra Susīma* in four fascicles was translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao;
the *Sūtra on the Original Acts of the Jeweled Necklace* in two fascicles was translated in the Taishi era of the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa;
and the *Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Sun-Transcending Radiance* in two fascicles was translated during the Former Qin dynasty by Zhu Fonian.
The *Candrottarā-dārikā-vyākaraṇa-sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taishi era of the Jin dynasty;
the *Antarābhava-sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty;
and the *Sumerugarbha-sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by Zhu Fonian in Chang’an during the Former Qin period.
During the Qi dynasty, Yaśas and Fazhi co-translated the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi Sūtra* in two fascicles (or three fascicles).
During the Hongshi era of the Later Qin, Kumārajīva translated the *Mahābherī-haraka Sūtra* in two fascicles.
During the Song dynasty, Guṇavarman translated the *Sūtra on the Essential Collection of All Buddhas* in two fascicles at Yangzhou.
*The Mañjuśrī-buddhakṣetra-vyūha-sūtra*, two fascicles, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty;

translated by Dharmarakṣa at Luoyang in the Yongxi era of the Jin dynasty. *The Suvikrāntavikrami-paripṛcchā-anuttara-viśuddha-piṇḍapāta-sūtra*, two fascicles—also titled *The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Resolving All Dharmas as Like an Illusion*—translated by Master Xiang in Nanhai Commandery during the Song dynasty. *The Mahāyāna-samatā-nirdeśa-sūtra*, two fascicles.
The *Sarvadharmāpravṛttinirdeśa-sūtra* (Two fascicles), translated by Jñānagupta and Seng’an during the Tianhe era of the Later Zhou;

the *Akṣobhyatathāgatasyavyūha-sūtra* (Two fascicles, or one), translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin—also known as the *Buddhakṣetraprasādapratibhāsa-bodhisattva-śikṣā-siddhi-sūtra*;
the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi-sūtra* (Three fascicles, or two), translated during the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa; and the *Padmavaktra-sūtra* (Two fascicles).
The *Kāśyapa Sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by Jñānayaśas during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui;
the *Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī Dhāraṇī Sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by Upaśūna during the Northern Wei period;
and the *Anuttarāśraya Sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by Saṃghavarman during the Liang dynasty.
The *Adbhutadharmaparyāya-sūtra* in two fascicles was translated by the śramaṇa Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty at Guangzhou;
the *Sūryavairocanasamādhi-sūtra* in one fascicle was translated by Tanying during the Southern Qi dynasty;
and the *Sudāna-jātaka-sūtra* in one fascicle was translated by Zhi Yao during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty.
One fascicle of the *Prince Mupo Jing*, translated by Fajian of the Later Qin;
one fascicle of the *Sūrata-sūtra*, translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Jin;
and one fascicle of the *Suvarṇavarṇa-rāja-sūtra*, translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Samādhi of Sole Testimony and Self-Vow*, one fascicle, translated during the Northern Wei dynasty by Dharmaruci;
also known as *The Scripture on the Tathāgata’s Self-Vow Samādhi*, translated during the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa;
*The Mahāmāyā Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated during the Southern Qi dynasty by Tanying; and *The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra*, one fascicle.
*The Tathāgata’s Sūtra of Skillful Means and Mantras*, one fascicle, translated by Buddhabhadra during the Yixi era of the Jin dynasty.
*The Śrīmālādevī Siṃhanāda Sūtra on the Great Skillful Means of the One Vehicle*, one fascicle, translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaishuang era of the Sui dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Sumati*, one fascicle—also titled simply *The Sumati Sūtra*—translated by Guṇabhadra at Yangzhou during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Rare and Extraordinary Measurement of Merit*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin Dynasty;
*The Sūtra of the Brahmin Girl Śirīṣā*, one fascicle, translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui Dynasty;
*The Sūtra of the Prediction for Kṣemapati*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin Dynasty.
One fascicle of the *Moon-Bright Bodhisattva Sūtra*, translated by Dharmaruci during the Northern Wei dynasty;
one fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Extinction of Darkness in the Ten Directions*, translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty;
and one fascicle of the *Pumenpin Sūtra*, translated by Zhu Fahu during the Yuanxi era of the Jin dynasty.
*The Sutra on the Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; *The Sutra of the Heart-Clarification*, one fascicle.
These two sutras were translated during the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu.
*The Scripture on the Moon-Lamp Samādhi*, one fascicle; also titled *The Ten Deeds of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva* or *The Scripture on the Attainment of Wisdom Samādhi*;

translated by Xian Gong during the Song dynasty. *The Scripture Spoken by the Bodhisattva Acintyārthaprabha*, one fascicle; also titled *The Scripture of the Childlike Bodhisattva Acintyārthaprabha*; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture on Mañjuśrī’s Inquiry into the Bodhisattva Stations*, one fascicle; also titled *The Scripture on the Inquiry into Stations*.

*The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on Prince Virtuous Light*, one fascicle, translated during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han by Zhi Chen; also known as *The Sutra on Rāṣṭrapāla Asking about Prince Virtuous Light*, translated in the Taishi era of the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu.
*The Sutra on the Merit of Offering Lamps*, one fascicle, also known as *The Sutra on Lighting Lamps*, translated during the Qi dynasty by Yasha.
*The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Rebuke of Lust*, one fascicle.
*The Scripture on the Desire for Birth as a Human Being*, one fascicle, translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin;
*The Scripture on Where People Come From*, one fascicle, translated by An Shigao during the reign of Emperor Huan of the Later Han;

*The Scripture on Neither Increasing nor Decreasing*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty; *The Scripture of the Buddha’s Words*, one fascicle; *The Scripture of the Jewel Casket Without Letters*, one fascicle. The above three scriptures were translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty.

*The Tathāgata’s Lion’s Roar Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated during the Later Wei dynasty by Bodhiruci together with Buddhasanta. *The Sūtra of the Ten Dharmas*, one fascicle; translated at Yangzhou during the Putong era of the Liang dynasty by Saṃghavarman. *The Sūtra on Entering the Seal of Non-Definitive Concentration*, one fascicle; translated during the Later Wei dynasty by Bodhiruci. *The Sūtra of the Names of the Twelve Buddhas*, one fascicle; translated during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui dynasty by Jñānagupta. *The Sūtra of Māra’s Rebellion*, one fascicle; translated during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa. *The Sūtra for Saving Those Studying the Vaipulya*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Fifty Circumstances of the Bodhisattva’s Practice*, one fascicle—these two sūtras were translated during the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa.
*The Sutra on the Inner Treasury of a Hundred Jewels*, one fascicle;
translated by Zhi Chen during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han. *The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle;
translated by Vinītāruci during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui. *The Sutra on the Original Vows Asked by Maitreya Bodhisattva*, one fascicle.
*Mañjuśrī-bhāṣita-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty;
*Dṛḍhamātṛ-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by Mandaraka during the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty;
*Saddharma-karmapatha-nirdeśa-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by Yaśas during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Birthplace of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle, translated during the reign of Yao Xing of the Later Qin;

also known as the *Carmavastu-sūtra*. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Way under the Tree*, one fascicle; also known as the *Svāgata-sūtra*, the *Svāgama-sūtra*, or the *Bodhivṛkṣa-samādhi-sūtra*.
Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty. *The Jewel Net Sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Ratnajāla-kumāra-sūtra*.
*The Sutra of the Names of One Hundred Buddhas*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty;
*The Sutra of Immeasurable Meanings*, one fascicle, translated by Yaśas during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui;
*The Sutra on Contemplating Maitreya’s Ascent to Tuṣita Heaven*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmagatayaśas in Yangzhou during the Jianyuan era of the Southern Qi.
*The Sūtra on the Contemplation of Amitāyus*, one fascicle, translated during the Northern Liang dynasty by Juqu An-yang Hou;
*The Sūtra on the Method of Practice for Contemplating Samantabhadra Bodhisattva*, one fascicle, translated in the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty by Jñānayaśas at Yangzhou;
*The Amoghapāśa Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated in the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty by Dharmamitra at Yangzhou.
*The Scripture on Contemplating the Two Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata*, one fascicle, translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui dynasty;
*The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī for Invoking Avalokiteśvara to Eliminate and Subdue Poisonous Harm*, one fascicle, translated by Kālayaśas during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty;
*The Scripture on the Eleven-Faced Avalokiteśvara*, one fascicle, translated by Zhu Nantide, a foreign merchant chief from the Western Regions during the Song dynasty.
One fascicle of the *Avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-vyākaraṇa-sūtra*, translated during the Later Zhou dynasty by Jñānagupta;
one fascicle of the *Mṛgī-mātṛ-sūtra*, translated during the Song dynasty by Dharmakṣema at Yangzhou;
and one fascicle of the *Mṛgaputra-sūtra*, translated during the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa.
*Jue kong zai huan jing* (Sutra on Eliminating Fearful Calamities), one fascicle, translated by Zhi Qian during the Jianxing era of the Wu dynasty;
*Ba jixiang jing* (Sutra of the Eight Auspicious Ones), one fascicle, translated by Bo Yan during the Wei dynasty;

*Wenshi xiyu zhong seng jing* (Sutra on Bathing the Assembly of Monks in the Warm Chamber), one fascicle, translated by Guṇabhadra at Jingzhou during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty; and *Si bukede jing* (Sutra on the Four Unobtainables), one fascicle—these latter two sutras were translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
*Zhude fudian jing* (Sutra on the Fields of Merit for All Virtuous Ones), one fascicle—also known as *Fudian jing*—translated by Faju and Fali during the Jin dynasty;
*Chujia gongde jing* (Sutra on the Merit of Leaving Home), one fascicle, translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty;
*Dafangguang shilun jing* (The Great Vaipulya Sutra of the Ten Wheels), ten fascicles.

Either the *Mahā-upāya-kauśalya-pitṛ-ṛṇa-pratyupakāra-sūtra* in eight fascicles; the *Saptabuddha-sūtra* in seven fascicles; the *Tathāgata-gotra-utpatti-sūtra* in four fascicles, or three or two fascicles;

the *Bodhisattva-pūrva-caryā-sūtra* in three fascicles; the *Acintya-guṇa-sūtra* in two fascicles—also known as the *Guṇa-sūtra*; the *Mahā-maṅgala-artha-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in two fascicles, or four fascicles;

the *Bodhisattva-svapna-sūtra* in two fascicles; the *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-sūtra* in two fascicles; the *Ratna-rāja-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* in two fascicles; the *Dharma-dhātu-svabhāva-avikalpa-sūtra* in two fascicles; and the *Guhyapāda* [Sūtra].
The *Malla-sūtra*, two fascicles; the *Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-dhāraṇī-puṇya-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Mahāvaipulya-tathāgata-rahasya-garbha-sūtra*, one fascicle;
the *Subāhu-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, two fascicles; the *Bodhisattva-caryā-sūtra*, one fascicle (also known as the *Ugraparipṛcchā-kāyagatāsati-sūtra*);
the *Bodhisattva-dehaparityāga-vyāghrī-caitya-pratyaya-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Sarvadānapati-caryā-dānapāramitā-sūtra*, one fascicle; and the *Bimbisāra-rāja-buddha-upasaṃkramaṇa-pūjā-sūtra*.
*Sūtra* in one fascicle; *Sālavatī-sūtra* in one fascicle; *Mahārtha-sūtra* in one fascicle; *Rājaputra Vilāra-sūtra* in one fascicle;
*Gṛhapati Ghosita-sūtra* in one fascicle; *Gṛhapati Dharmasena-patnī-sūtra* in one fascicle; *Sarvajñajyotis-rṣi-maitracitta-hetupratyaya-amāṃsa-bhakṣaṇa-sūtra* in one fascicle;
*Mañjuśrī-parinirvāṇa-sūtra* in one fascicle; *Siṃhacandra-buddha-jātaka-sūtra* in one fascicle; *Amitābha-dundubhi-nirghoṣa-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in one fascicle; *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi*.
*Jīng* (Sūtra), one fascicle; *Vajrasamādhi-bhāvasvabhāva-viśuddhy-avināśy-aniruddha-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Vajra-viśuddhi-sūtra*;
*Ratnakūṭa-samādhi-mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-dharmakāya-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Sahasrabuddha-nidāna-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Aṣṭabuddhanāma-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Aṣṭamaṅgala-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Aṣṭasūrya-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Daśamaṅgala-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Bhadramukha-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Bhadramukhā-devī-sūtra*; *Gambhīra-mahāpariṇāmanā-sūtra*.
*The Sūtra on the Five Meritorious Virtues of the Wise*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Illusionist Rishi Renxian*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light*, one fascicle.
There are fourteen separate works of Mahāyāna Vinaya totaling thirty fascicles.
*The Buddha-piṭaka Sūtra*, four fascicles; *The Upāsaka-śīla Sūtra*, ten fascicles (or five fascicles); these constitute the precepts for lay bodhisattvas.

During the Northern Liang period, Dharmakṣema, together with Huìsōng and others, translated: *Mahāvaipulya-triśikṣā-sūtra*, three fascicles; *Dharmapada-samādhi-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Bodhisattvādhyātma-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Samantabhadra-bodhisattva-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Bodhisattva-upavāsa-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Vimalakarma-āvaraṇa-viśuddhi-sūtra*, one fascicle. Single-text Mahāyāna treatises: forty-two works totaling one hundred and eleven fascicles. The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, one hundred fascicles, translated by Kumārajīva at Cháng'ān during the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
The *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, twelve fascicles, translated by Ratnamati and Bodhiruci together at Luòyáng during the Yǒngmíng era of the Later Wèi dynasty. Compiled by the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna.

The *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, fourteen fascicles, translated by Ratnamati and Bodhiruci together at Luòyáng during the Yǒngmíng era of the Later Wèi dynasty. Compiled by the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna.
One fascicle of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śāstra*, translated by Kumārajīva during the Later Qin dynasty;
one fascicle of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-pūrvāstitva-adhunānāstitva-gāthā-śāstra*, translated by Dharmaprabha;
and ten fascicles (or nine, or five) of the *Maitreyaparipṛcchā-sūtra-śāstra*, translated by Paramārtha at Guangzhou during the Chen dynasty.

Translated during the Northern Wei period by Bodhiruci: the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra-śāstra* in four fascicles; the *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra* in three fascicles; the *Suvikrāntavikrāmi-paripṛcchā-sūtra-śāstra* in three or four fascicles; the *Triskandhaka-sūtra-śāstra* in one fascicle; the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-śāstra* in one fascicle; the *Dharmacakra-pravartana-sūtra-śāstra* in one fascicle; the *Bodhisattvaguhyakapilottara-dharmaparyāya-śāstra* in one fascicle; the *Amitāyurdhyāna-sūtra-śāstra* in one fascicle; and the *Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-bodhicitta-śāstra* in two fascicles (also known as the *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra-śāstra*). These nine treatises were translated during the Northern Wei period by Bodhiruci.
The *Mahāvyūha-śāstra* (Great Ornament Treatise), ten fascicles or fifteen fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa;

translated during the Later Qin dynasty by Kumārajīva. The *Buddhadhātu-śāstra* (Treatise on Buddha-nature), four fascicles, translated during the Chen dynasty by Paramārtha. The *Mahāpuruṣa-śāstra* (Treatise on the Great Man), two fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Āryadeva.
The *Madhyāntavibhāga-śāstra* in three fascicles, translated during the Northern Liang dynasty by Daotai;
the *Vigraha-vyāvartanī* in one fascicle, translated during the Chen dynasty by Paramārtha;
and the *Buddha-abhidharma-śāstra* in two fascicles, translated during the Later Wei dynasty by Gautama Saṃghadeva.
*Śālistambasūtra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Rice Seedling Sutra), one fascicle, translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty;
*Madhyamaka-śāstra* (Treatise on the Middle Way), four fascicles, translated by Gautama Kumārajīva at Chang’an during the Later Qin dynasty;
*Anupūrva-madhyamaka-śāstra* (Gradual Treatise on the Middle Way), two fascicles.

*The Scripture of the Daughter Nāgadattā*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *The Scripture on the Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva Nāgadatta*, one fascicle. The above two scriptures are translations of the same original text with different translations.
*Śānti-putra-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Fa-jian during the Western Qin period. *Bodhisattva-śānti-sūtra*, one fascicle. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*Anupūrva-upāya-kauśalya-sūtra*, two fascicles; also titled *Pusa-zhuan-nüshen-jing*, one fascicle; translated by Zhu Fa-hu during the Jin period. *Lai-yingluo-zhuangyan-fangbian-jing*, one fascicle; translated by Fa-hai during the Song period. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.
*The Scripture on Understanding Fundamental Birth and Death*, one fascicle; translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty. *The Scripture on the Rice Seedling*, one fascicle.

The above two scriptures are different translations of the same original text. *The Mahāvaipulya Bodhisattva Ten Grounds Scripture*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *The Scripture on Adorning the Bodhicitta*, one fascicle; translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty. The above two scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sutra on Having No Hopes*, one fascicle; also known as the *Sutra on the Elephant’s Stride*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *The Sutra on the Elephant’s Armpit*, one fascicle. The above two sutras are the same text translated differently.

*Mahāvaipulya-sūtra-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmaruci during the Later Wei period. *Parivarta-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of the Northern Wei period. The two sūtras above are the same text with different translations.

*Mahāyāna-ārya-prajñā-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Maitreya-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmaruci during the Later Wei period. The two sūtras above are the same text with different translations.

*Huiyin Sanmei Jing* (The Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Seal of Wisdom), one fascicle; translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty. *Rulai Zhinyin Jing* (The Sūtra on the Tathāgata’s Seal of Wisdom), one fascicle.

The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text. *Fangdeng Niepan Jing* (The Vaipulya Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra), two fascicles; translated by Buddhabhadra together with Faxian during the Jin dynasty. *Aiqi Jing* (The Sūtra of Lamentation), two fascicles. *Sijuntongzi Jing* (The Sūtra of the Four Youthful Disciples), three fascicles; translated by Jñānagupta and others during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty. The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Mahāmegha-pravarṣaṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Jñānagupta during the Later Zhou period. *Mahāmegha-cakra-sūtra*, two fascicles; translated by Jñāya during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui dynasty. The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Scripture on the High King of All Dharmas*, one fascicle; translated by [Dharmaruci] during the Xinghe era of the Later Wei. *The Scripture on the Heroic King of All Dharmas*, one fascicle. The above two scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Jueding zongchi jing* (Sūtra on the Decisive Dhāraṇī), two fascicles; also titled *Jue zongchi jing*. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty. *Bafu jing* (Sūtra on Slandering the Buddha), one fascicle. Translated by [Dharmaruci] during the Later Wei dynasty. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.
*The Sūtra of the Buddha Kṣīrarasmi*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Vatsiputriya*, one fascicle.

The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text. *The Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, thirty fascicles; translated by Mokṣala together with Zhu Shulan and others during the Western Jin dynasty. *The Praśāntaviniścayaprakhya-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, ten fascicles (or fifteen fascicles); translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty. The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sutra of the Vast, Sublime, Pure, and Non-retrogressive Wheel*, six fascicles (or four fascicles), translated by the śramaṇa Zhìyán together with Bǎoyún during the Yuánjiā era of the Song dynasty. *The Sutra of the Non-retrogressive Dharma-Wheel*, four fascicles; *The Sutra on the Avivartiya*, three fascicles (or four fascicles), translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Tàikāng era of the Jìn dynasty. The above three sutras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sūtra of the Questions of Brahmā Viśeṣacintin*, four fascicles; translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Questions of Brahmā Cittamatī*, four fascicles (or six fascicles); also titled *The Equal Mastery over All Dharmas* or *The Adornment of the Buddha-dharma*; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Questions of Brahmā Viśeṣacintin*, six fascicles; translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. The above three sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*The Sūtra on the Adornment of Wisdom that Transcends the Realms of All Buddhas*, one fascicle; translated by Mandaraka and Saṃghabhadra during the Liang dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Entrance into the Realms of All Buddhas through the Radiance of the Tathāgata’s Adorned Wisdom*, two fascicles; translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei period. *The Sūtra on the Adornment of the Radiance of Wisdom that Transcends the Realms of All Buddhas*, one fascicle. The above three sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*The Scripture on the Youth Candraprabha* (Fóshuō yuèguāng tóngzi jīng), one fascicle; there is another fascicle of the same title that is shorter and incomplete. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin Dynasty. *The Scripture of Śroṇakoṭiviṃśa* (Shēnrì jīng), one fascicle. *The Scripture of the Elder Guhagupta* (Déhù zhǎngzhě jīng), two fascicles. Translated by Yaśas during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui. The three scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.

*The Buddha’s Bequeathed Sun-Maṇi Jewel Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Zhi Chen during the Guanghe era of the Later Han dynasty. *The Great Jewel Accumulation Sūtra*, one fascicle. *The Mahāyāna Jewel Adornment Sūtra*, one fascicle. The above three sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty at Śrāvastī. *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty at the Jeta Grove. The above three sūtras are translations of the same original text.

*Mahāvaipulya Śikhara-rāja Sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Vimalakīrti-putra-praśna Sūtra* or the *Mahāyāna Śikhara-rāja Sūtra*, one fascicle; and the *Susiddhi-kumāra Sūtra*, two fascicles. Translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui Dynasty. The three sūtras above are different translations of the same original text.

*The Elder’s Vinaya Sūtra* (one fascicle), also known as *The Vinaya Sūtra* or *The Sūtra of the Departing Youth* (one fascicle); translated by Zhī Fǎdù during the Jìn dynasty; and *The Buddha-spoken Sūtra of the Departing Bodhisattva* (one fascicle), also known as *The Sūtra of Departure*. These three sūtras above are the same original text with different translations.

*The Sūtra on Mañjuśrī Asking about Bodhi*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra on the Non-Practice of Bodhi*. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Summit of Mount Gayā*, one fascicle. Translated by Bodhiruci during the era of the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Elephant Head Monastery*, one fascicle. Translated by Vinitaruci during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui dynasty. The above three sūtras are translations of the same original text.

*The Sutra on Contemplating the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination under the Pippala Tree*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *Sutra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination Heard in the City*, one fascicle; translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty. *Sutra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*, one fascicle; translated by Guṇavidi during the Yongming era of the Southern Qi dynasty. The above three sutras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sūtra on the Questions of the Householder Ugga*, one fascicle; translated by Kang Senghai during the Wei dynasty. *The Dharma-mirror Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by An Gong and Fotiao during the Later Han dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Practice as Questioned by the Householder Uggarāta*, one fascicle; translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty. The above three sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*Wúliàng qīngjìng píngděng jué jīng*, two fascicles; translated by Bó Yán during the Wei dynasty. *Āmítuó jīng*, two fascicles; translated by Zhī Qiān during the Huangwǔ era of the Wu dynasty. *Wúliàng shòu jīng*, two fascicles; translated by Zhú Fǎhù during the Yǒngjiā era of the Jìn dynasty. The above three sutras are different translations of the same original text.

*Daoxing Banruo Boluomi Jing* (The Perfection of Wisdom Sutra on the Course of Practice), one fascicle; translated by Zhi Chen during the Guanghe era of the Later Han dynasty. *New Daoxing Jing* (New Sutra on the Course of Practice), ten fascicles or seven fascicles; also known as the *Xin Xiaopin Jing* (New Shorter Prajñāpāramitā Sutra); translated by Zhu Fahu during the Taishi era of the Jin dynasty. *Xiaopin Jing* (Shorter Prajñāpāramitā Sutra), ten fascicles, seven fascicles, or eight fascicles; translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty. *Mingdu Jing* (Sutra of the Clear Crossing), six fascicles or four fascicles; also known as the *Damingdu Wujijing* (Great Sutra of the Infinite Clear Crossing); translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty. The above four sutras are translations of the same original text.

*The Scripture on the Transformation of Women*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Daughter in the Womb Heard the Dharma*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Treasury of the Womb Spoken by Dharmakṣema during the Southern Qi Dynasty*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Immaculate Virtuous Woman*, one fascicle. The above four scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Guan xukongzang pusa jing* (Sūtra on the Contemplation of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha), one fascicle; translated by Dharmamitra in Yangzhou during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty. *Xukongzang pusa jing* (Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva Sūtra), one fascicle; translated by Buddhayaśas during the Later Qin dynasty. *Xukongzang shenzhou jing* (Ākāśagarbha Divine Mantra Sūtra), one fascicle; translated by Buddhayaśas during the Later Qin dynasty. *Xukong ying jing* (Ākāśagarbha Sūtra), two fascicles; translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui dynasty. The above four sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sūtra on the Secret Retention of Immeasurable Gateways*, one fascicle; translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Retention that Produces Immeasurable Gateways*, one fascicle; translated by Buddhabhadra during the Yuanxi era of the Jin dynasty. *The Ānanda-mukha-nihāra Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Buddhayaśas during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Immeasurable Gateways Dhāraṇī for Subduing Māras*, one fascicle; translated by Guṇadharman at Jingzhou during the Daming era of the Song dynasty. *The Śāriputra Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle. *The Sūtra on the Sole Birth of Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle; translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui dynasty. The above six sūtras are the same text with different translations.
*The Sutra of the Three Turnings of the Previous Life*, one fascicle; *The Sutra of the Silver-Colored Woman*, one fascicle. These two sutras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Huahou Sutra*, one fascicle; *The Sutra of the Crown Prince’s Brush Protection*, one fascicle. These two sutras are different translations of the same original text.
The *Saddharmopāya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Vajraguhya-samantamukha-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle. These two sūtras are the same text translated differently.

*The Scripture on King Ajātaśatru Receiving the Prediction*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on Plucking Flowers and Contravening the King’s Edict to Present Them to the Buddha and Receiving the Prediction*, one fascicle.

These two scriptures above are translations of the same original text. *The Scripture on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrīḍita*, one fascicle; *The Flower-Arrayed Dhāraṇī Scripture*, one fascicle; *The Flower-Cluster Dhāraṇī Scripture*, one fascicle. These three scriptures above are translations of the same original text.

The *Jianbei yiqiezhide jing* (Sutra on Gradually Preparing for All-Wisdom Virtue) in five fascicles is a separate translation by Zhu Fahu during the Yuankang era of the Jin dynasty of the "Ten Stages" chapter (*Daśabhūmika*) of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. The *Shizhu jing* (Sutra of the Ten Abidings) in four fascicles is also a separate translation by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty of the same "Ten Stages" chapter.
The *Luomojia jing* (Ratnamati Sutra) in three fascicles is the "Entering the Dharma Realm" chapter (*Gandavyūha*).
The *Śraddhābalādhānāvatāramudrāsūtra* in five fascicles was separately translated by Qifu Rensheng and Shengjian during the Western Qin dynasty; it is a separate chapter of the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*.

The *Tathāgatotpattisambhavanirdeśasūtra* in four fascicles—also known as the *Tathāgatanirmāṇasambhavasūtra*—was separately translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty; it is the *Tathāgatagarbha-niṣyanda-parivarta*.
The *Lokottaraparivartasūtra* in six fascicles was separately translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Yuankang era of the Jin dynasty; it is the *Lokottara-parivarta*.

In the Yuankang era of the Jin dynasty, Zhu Fahu separately translated the *Bodhisattva-daśabhūmi-caryā-prakaraṇa* in one fascicle; this is the *Bodhisattva-mūla-karma-daśabhūmi-sūtra* in one fascicle, which contains the *Śuddhacaryā-prakaraṇa* and an abbreviated version of the *Daśabhūmi-prakaraṇa* lacking its verses.

During the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty, Zhi Qian separately translated the *Sarvabodhisattva-buddha-mūla-karma-sūtra* in one fascicle, which contains the *Śuddhacaryā-prakaraṇa*. These nine scriptures above are distinct translations of individual chapters from the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*.

The *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* in six fascicles comprises the first sixteen fascicles of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, ending with the "Chapter on the Questions of the Great Assembly. It was translated by the śramaṇa Faxian during the Yixi era of the Jin dynasty. The above-mentioned scripture is a distinct translation of a separate chapter from the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*.
The *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra* (Great Compassion Sutra) in eight fascicles is the "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīśvara," or alternatively in seven fascicles;

it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Yuankang era of the Jin dynasty. The *Ākāśagarbha-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (Sutra of the Questions of Ākāśagarbha) in six fascicles is the "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha," or alternatively in eight fascicles;

it was translated by Shengjian during the reign of Qifu Renxiao of the Western Qin. The *Ratnaśikhara-bodhisattva-sūtra* (Sutra of the Bodhisattva Ratnaśikhara) in two fascicles is the "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Ratnaśikhara," also titled the *Bodhisattva-viśuddhacaryā-sūtra* (Sutra of the Pure Conduct of Bodhisattvas).
The *Aksayamatinirdeśa-sūtra* in seven fascicles, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Yongxi era of the Jin dynasty;

this is the *Akṣayamati-parivarta*, or alternatively, the *Akṣayamati-sūtra* in four fascicles, also translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Yongjia era of the Jin dynasty; this is likewise the *Aksayamatinirdeśa-sūtra*;
and the *Anabhilāpya-bodhisattva-sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taishi era of the Jin dynasty.

The *Ratnāvalī-sūtra* (寶女經) in four fascicles, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty; alternatively, it exists in three fascicles as the "Chapter on the Precious Woman" (*Ratnāvalī-parivarta*), translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty.
The above seven sūtras are distinct translations of individual chapters from the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*.

The *Saṃtati-vimokṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle; this is a portion of the *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra*. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty. The *Vibhaṅga-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty. These two sūtras above are alternative translations of specific chapters from the *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra*.
*The Sutra on Setting Aside the Alms Bowl*, one fascicle. The above sutra is a distinct translation of a separate chapter from the *Puchao jing*.
*The Sutra of the Bodhisattva Badatā*, one fascicle; these are the first four chapters. The above sutra is a distinct translation of a separate chapter from the *Banzhou sanmei jing*.

The Mahāyāna Vinaya Re-translated in Three Sections, three fascicles; *The Sūtra of the Extensive Vinaya of Purity*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin Dynasty; *The Mañjuśrī-viśuddha-vinaya-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin Dynasty; *The Sūtra of the Questions of Śāntasvara*, one fascicle, translated by Fahai during the Song Dynasty. The above three vinayas are different translations of the same original text.

*Mahāyānasaṃparigraha-śāstra* (The Treatise on the Compendium of the Mahāyāna), eight fascicles, five volumes; *Mahāyānasaṃparigraha-bhāṣya* (The Commentary on the Compendium of the Mahāyāna), twelve fascicles, translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty. *Mahāyānasaṃparigraha-bhāṣya*, ten fascicles (or fifteen fascicles), translated by Paramārtha at Guangzhou during the Chen dynasty. The two treatises above are translations of the same original text with different versions.

*Bo-sa-di-chi lun* (Bodhisattvabhūmiviniścaya-śāstra), eight fascicles or ten fascicles; translated by Dharmakṣema during the Northern Liang period. *Pusa shanjie jing* (Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra), ten fascicles; also known as the *Pusa badi jing*; translated by Guṇavarman in Yangzhou during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty. The above two treatises are the same original text with different translations.

*Mahāyānasaṃgraha-mūla-śāstra*, two fascicles; translated by Buddhanta during the Northern Wei period. *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-śāstra*, three fascicles; translated by Paramārtha at Guangzhou during the Chen period. The above two treatises are the same original text with different translations.

*Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle; “Consciousness-only has no external objects,” translated by Gautama Dharmaruci during the Northern Wei period. *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle; “The Ultimate Path is Not Shared with Others,” translated by Paramārtha during the Chen period. The two treatises above are translations of the same original text.

Re-translations of Hinayāna Sūtras: ninety-four works in one hundred and twelve fascicles. *Āraṇyaka-caryā-dhyāna-dharma-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty. *Dhyāna-samādhi-sūtra*, two fascicles (or three); these two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Śīkṣāsamuccaya-sūtra* (The Sutra on the Renunciation of Head-Counsel), one fascicle; also titled *Prince Aṣṭāviṃśati-nakṣatra-sūtra* or *Prince Vyāghra-karṇa-sūtra*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Yongjia era of the Jin dynasty. *Mātanga-sūtra*, three fascicles (or two fascicles). The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Benxiang yizhi jing* (Sūtra on the Fundamental Characteristics Leading to the Ultimate), one fascicle; translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty. *Yuanben zhi jing* (Sūtra on the Conditions Leading to the Ultimate), one fascicle. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*Anan wen shifo jixiong jing* (Sūtra on Ānanda Asking about the Auspiciousness and Inauspiciousness of Serving the Buddha), one fascicle; translated by Fa Jian during the reign of Qifu Ren of the Western Qin. *Foshuo anan fenbie jing* (Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on Ānanda’s Discrimination), one fascicle; also known as the *Fenbie jing*. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*The Sūtra on the Retribution of Sinful Karma*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra on the Differentiation of Karmic Retribution* or *The Sūtra on the Distinctions of Karmic Retribution*, one fascicle. Translated by Fǎzhì during the Kaihuáng era of the Great Sui dynasty. The two sūtras above are the same text with different translations.
The *Sūtra of the Five Mothers and Sons*, one fascicle; the *Śamīra Sūtra*, one fascicle—these two sūtras are translations of the same original text with different translations.

The *Asudā Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Yuye Sūtra* (also titled *The Sūtra of the Elder Visiting the Buddha to Speak of His Son’s Wife’s Lack of Reverence*; also titled *The Sūtra of the Seven Wives*)—these two sūtras are translations of the same original text with different translations.

The *Ullambana Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Jianla Sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Sūtra on the Four Classes of Disciples Offering the Jianla Ritual after the Parinirvāṇa*; and the *Bao'en Fengcun Sūtra*, one fascicle. These three sūtras are translations of the same original text with different translations.

The *Maudgalyāyanī-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Maudgalyāyanī-sūtra* or the *Sūtra on Ānanda Being Cursed by a Malevolent Spirit*. The *Sūtra on Maudgalyāyanī Resolving Six Matters within the Body*, one fascicle. These two sūtras are translations of the same original text with different translations.

*The Sūtra on Cause and Effect in Past and Present*, four fascicles; translated by Guṇabhadra during the Song dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Auspicious Responses of the Prince’s Original Arising*, two fascicles; translated by Zhi Qian during the Jianxing era of the Wu dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Original Arising of Practice*, two fascicles; translated jointly by Dharmaphala and Zhu Dalie during the Later Han dynasty. The above three sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Zá zàng jīng* (Saṃyukta-piṭaka Sūtra), one fascicle; translated during the Jin dynasty by Buddhabhadra together with Faxian. *Guǐ wèn Mùlián jīng* (Sūtra on the Ghosts Questioning Maudgalyāyana), one fascicle. *Èguǐ bào yìng jīng* (Sūtra on the Retribution of Hungry Ghosts), one fascicle; also titled *Mùlián shuō dìyù èguǐ yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Hells and Hungry Ghosts Spoken by Maudgalyāyana). The above three sūtras are translations of the same original text.
*Vaiḍūryarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle;
separately translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *Aṅgulimālīya-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Aṅgulimāla-sūtra*;
separately translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *Parvata-parivartana-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Malla-parvata-parivartana-sūtra*.
*Samajātaka-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated separately by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty; also known as *Sūmāgadhāvadāna-sūtra*, *Dharmanandin-rāja-sūtra*, or *Bandhumant-rāja-sūtra*.
*Mahāprajāpatī-parinirvāṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by Zhu Lüyan during the Wu dynasty; also known as *Buddhamātṛ-parinirvāṇa-sūtra*.
*Śraddhā-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by Juqu An-yang Hou at Yangzhou during the Song dynasty; also known as *Gṛhapati-Śraddha-sūtra* or *Triśaraṇa-pañcaśīla-maitrī-nirveda-guṇa-sūtra*.
